pathways.name: Artificial Intelligence
pathways.description: The study of simulating intelligent behavior in computers, at the intersection of programming, data science, mathematical reasoning, creative problem solving, and ethics. Students use professional software-development tools and processes to build real-world AI applications with machine learning.

pathways.name: Cloud Computing
pathways.description: Cloud computing concepts, core services, security, architecture, and support: designing and deploying a virtual private network, building a scalable cloud environment, safe use of big data, and cloud best practices. The pathway was developed with input from AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft, Accenture, and NCR.

pathways.name: Computer Science
pathways.description: Prepares students for entry-level, technical, and professional IT careers in the design, development, implementation, and maintenance of systems and software, with emphasis on computational thinking: developing computational artifacts, abstracting, analyzing problems, communicating, and collaborating.

pathways.name: Entrepreneurship
pathways.description: Recognizing a business opportunity and starting, operating, and maintaining a business: planning, organizing, coordinating, and controlling resources, along with the statutes and regulations that affect businesses, families, and individuals.

pathways.name: Financial Services
pathways.description: Business ownership foundations plus methods for measuring the financial performance of financial institutions and investments: banking, investing, insurance and risk management, and ethics and fraud in banking.

pathwayNote: Business & Computer Science covers courses numbered 06, 07, and 11.4 (Business Management & Administration, Finance, Information Technology), including AP Computer Science. Marketing pathways at Denmark are certified separately.

fblaRecruitment: Denmark FBLA is open to students of every interest: finance, entrepreneurship, technology, communication, leadership, education, and more. Officers recruit all year through Instagram, Remind, announcements, classroom visits, and Rush Week, and follow up personally with every interested student.

fblaPlan.title: DHS FBLA Chapter Member Recruitment Project Plan
fblaPlan.goal: Increase DHS FBLA membership and get more students actively involved in the chapter by reaching as many students as possible, making FBLA easy to understand, and giving students a reason to join and stay involved.

steps.title: Prepare for recruitment
steps.text: Officers ready membership information, meeting dates, competitive event information, and ways to get involved, plus Instagram posts, Remind messages, flyers, announcements, and classroom outreach.

steps.title: Push recruitment
steps.text: FBLA is promoted repeatedly through Instagram, Remind, announcements, classroom visits, flyers, and personal conversations. Members invite friends. During Rush Week, the chapter points system rewards attendance at activities, meetings, and recruitment events.

steps.title: Reach more students
steps.text: Outreach goes beyond students already interested in business, to students interested in finance, entrepreneurship, technology, communication, leadership, education, and other areas.

steps.title: Follow up with interested students
steps.text: Officers answer questions, send reminders about deadlines and meetings, and personally reach out to students who showed interest but have not finished joining.

steps.title: Make new members feel involved
steps.text: New members immediately receive communication channels, meeting and competition information, and help finding an area of FBLA that interests them.

steps.title: Push competition participation
steps.text: New members are introduced to competitive events, encouraged to choose one that fits their strengths, and reminded about competition meetings, deadlines, and preparation.

steps.title: Keep members active
steps.text: Recruitment continues all year. Active members are recognized, and officers work to bring inactive members back to meetings and activities.

fblaPlan.tracking: Officers track new members, Rush Week participation, meeting attendance, competition participation, and event involvement throughout the year, using the chapter points tracker.
